questions.q: When should you reach for a Script Task or Script Component instead of a built-in task or transformation?
options: For every single task in a package, as a general replacement for built-in components
Only when the package needs to run faster
Never — Script Tasks were removed from modern versions of SSIS
When the job isn't covered by anything in the Toolbox — like checking whether a file exists, parsing an unusual format, or calling an API with no SSIS connector
questions.explain: Script Tasks and Script Components exist for the jobs that don't map to a common, well-defined built-in task or transformation.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Script Task and a Script Component?
options: A Script Component can only be used as a destination, never a source or transform
A Script Task lives on the Control Flow and runs once per execution; a Script Component lives on the Data Flow and runs once per row
There is no difference — they are two names for the same object
A Script Task only supports VB, while a Script Component only supports C#
questions.explain: Script Task is a control-flow task (runs once per execution/iteration); Script Component is a data-flow component that runs once per row and can act as a source, transformation, or destination.

questions.q: What development environment do both Script Tasks and Script Components use to write and edit code?
options: SQL Server Management Studio's Query Editor
Visual Studio Code
VSTA (Visual Studio Tools for Applications)
Notepad, launched directly from the Toolbox
questions.explain: Both open into VSTA, the Visual Studio-based code editor built into SSIS Designer for writing Script Task/Component code.

questions.q: In the example Script Task, what does setting `Dts.TaskResult = (int)ScriptResults.Failure;` actually do?
options: Deletes the file referenced by the FilePath variable
Immediately closes SSIS Designer
Reports failure back to the control flow, so the package can react (for example, stop or take a different path) based on the script's outcome
Has no effect unless the package is running in debug mode
questions.explain: TaskResult is how a Script Task reports Success or Failure back to the control flow that contains it, just like any other task.

questions.q: Before a Script Task's code can read a package variable through `Dts.Variables`, what must you configure first?
options: Convert the project to the project deployment model
List the variable in the Script Task Editor's ReadOnlyVariables (or ReadWriteVariables) property
Rename the variable to start with 'Dts.'
Nothing — every package variable is automatically available to every script with no configuration
questions.explain: A variable has to be explicitly listed in ReadOnlyVariables or ReadWriteVariables on the Script page before the script can access it through Dts.Variables.
